evals.prompt: I run marketing at a small literary publisher. Our monthly email newsletter 'The Shelf' — a staff book pick, a list of new releases, and a short author interview — has slipped from 31% to 22% open rate over the past year and clicks are flat. Use SCAMPER to come up with ideas to make it fresh again, and tell me which ones to try first.
evals.expected_output: Full SCAMPER session: framed goal, attributes, ideas under all 7 letters with bold ideas, scored shortlist, prioritized next steps with tests.
expectations: Output covers all seven SCAMPER letters (S, C, A, M, P, E, R) as distinct sections
Output explicitly lists the attributes/components of the newsletter that were examined (e.g. subject line, format, cadence, sections)
M section includes at least one Magnify AND at least one Minify idea
At least one idea per letter on average is labelled as bold/far-out
Includes a shortlist with explicit scoring or prioritization criteria (e.g. New/Useful/Feasible or impact/effort)
Each recommended idea has a concrete cheapest test (e.g. A/B subject line test) and a riskiest assumption or success signal
Recommendations address the open-rate problem specifically (subject line / sender / preview / timing), not only content inside the email

evals.prompt: here's the back-cover blurb for a debut psychological thriller ... give me 3 rewritten options.
evals.expected_output: Three finished rewritten blurbs, each labelled with the SCAMPER operator(s) behind it, cliches removed, a recommendation.
expectations: Provides exactly three (or at least three) complete rewritten blurbs ready to use
Each rewritten blurb is labelled with the SCAMPER operator(s) or strategy behind it
None of the rewrites use the original clichés 'Some secrets are better left buried', 'race against time', or 'won't be able to put down'
Recommends one option with a reason
Any invented plot specifics are flagged as placeholders for the editor to confirm
The three options are structurally different from each other (not just reworded versions of the same structure)

evals.prompt: Our online bookstore checkout is 5 steps: cart → create account → shipping address → payment → review & confirm. Mobile abandonment is around 70%. What could we eliminate, and what could we reverse or rearrange? Give me concrete changes.
evals.expected_output: Deep Eliminate and Reverse/Rearrange pass on checkout steps, concrete changes, prioritized, with tests and UX caveats.
expectations: Focuses on Eliminate and Reverse/Rearrange rather than running a full 7-letter session
Proposes eliminating forced account creation (guest checkout or post-purchase account)
Proposes at least one Rearrange idea that changes step order (e.g. account creation after payment, or shipping estimate in cart)
Includes at least one Reverse idea that inverts a role or assumption, not just reordering
Changes are prioritized (e.g. quick wins vs bigger bets)
Recommends testing/measuring the changes (A/B test, funnel metrics, usability test)
